Theme

Latin word

studium

studium, studiī n.

noun, second declension

pursuit, interest, activity one gives oneself to; bias, partisanship, favour for one side; zeal, eager and steady application, commitment; zeal, eagerness; eager goodwill, devotion to someone; interest, keenness; a pursuit; eagerness, will (to do something)

In this lexicon

  • activity

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Sen. 76: sunt pueritiae studia certa; Hor. S. 2.1.27–28: quot capitum vīvunt, totidem studiōrum mīlia

  • bias

    the recommended word · classical · Tac. Ann. 1.1: sine īrā et studiō

  • commitment

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Inv. 1.36: studium est animī assidua et vehemēns ad aliquam rem applicāta magnā cum voluntāte occupātiō (Lewis & Short); Cic. Sen. 22: modo permaneat studium et industria; Traupman 29: drive, enthusiasm; Traupman 310; Traupman 307

  • enthusiasm

    the recommended word · classical · Lewis & Short s.v. studium; Traupman 177: magnō cum studiō, with great enthusiasm; Traupman 410

  • favour

    also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 5.8.4: eximium et singulāre meum studium (Lewis & Short)

  • interest

    the recommended word · classical · Plin. Ep. 9.33.3: piscandī nāvigandī atque etiam natandī studiō tenētur; Cic. Fin. 5.5; M-O s.v. interest vb.; Traupman 333

  • motivation

    also used · classical · Quint. 1.3.8: studium discendī voluntāte, quae cōgī nōn potest, cōnstat
